passage:
The town bought its first electric bus. It was quieter than the old diesel buses and did not leave dark smoke behind.
Some riders liked it immediately. Others worried it would stop working on long routes. The driver explained that the bus had to be charged carefully every night, just like a phone, but on a much larger scale.
During the first month, the bus worked well except on one rainy day when charging equipment had a problem. The town learned that buying clean technology also means building support for it.
The electric bus was not magic. It was a step. A cleaner future still needs planning, repair, and patience.
